Identify and describe theoretical (expected) probabilities as being the likelihood of outcomes occurring under fair or unbiased conditions
Explain that observed probability is the relative frequency resulting from repeated trials of a simulation and determine observed probabilities
Explore relative frequencies by using a random number generator to repeat a chance experiment a number of times
Identify and describe the complement of an event
Verify that the sum of the probability of an event and its complement is a total of 1
Solve problems involving the probability of complementary events
Represent the possible outcomes for complementary events in various forms

answer.worked:
The scale shows a probability of $0.3$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Cards less than 3}&=0.3\times20\\\text{Cards less than 3}&=6\end{align*}$$

The initial probability is $\frac{6}{20}$. Let $x$ be the number of cards less than 3 added.

Add 8 cards.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{less than }3)&=\frac{6+8}{20+8}\\P(\text{less than }3)&=\frac{14}{28}\\P(\text{less than }3)&=\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$$

roll is equally likely to be either odd or even.

inlines.text: A die has faces numbered 1 to 6. The die is biased so that the number 6 will appear more often than each of the other numbers. The numbers 1 to 5 are equally likely to occur.
The die was rolled 1200 times and it was noted that the 6 appeared 450 times.
The probability of rolling the number 5 is expected to be
The number 6 is expected to appear 2 times as often as any other number.
The number 6 is expected to appear 3 times as often as any other number.
The probability of rolling an even number is expected to be equal to the probability of rolling an odd number.

answer.worked:
Use the observed relative frequency to estimate the probability of rolling a 6.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Relative frequency of 6} &= \frac{450}{1200}\\\text{Relative frequency of 6} &= \frac{3}{8}\\\text{Remaining estimated probability} &= 1-\frac{3}{8}\\\text{Remaining estimated probability} &= \frac{5}{8}\\\text{Estimated probability of each other number} &= \frac{5}{8}\div5\\\text{Estimated probability of each other number} &= \frac{1}{8}\\\text{Frequency ratio} &= \frac{3}{8}\div\frac{1}{8}\\\text{Frequency ratio} &= 3\end{align*}$$
The number 6 is expected to appear 3 times as often as any one other number.
Correct answer: C.

The Blue entry in the table gives $P(\text{blue})=19\%$.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{not green nor red})&=1-P(\text{green or red})\\P(\text{not green nor red})&=100\%-81\%\\P(\text{not green nor red})&=19\%\end{align*}$$

entries.description:
• A trial is a repetition of a chance experiment; rolling a die 100 times means 100 trials.
• Frequency is how often something happens.
• Expected frequency is how many times we think an event will happen in certain trials.
• Actual frequency may differ from expected frequency due to randomness.
• To calculate the expected frequency:
  1. Find the probability.
  2. Multiply number of trials by the probability.

Expected freq = Number of trials × Probability
f = np

entries.description:
A die has faces numbered 1 to 6. The die is biased so that the number 6 will appear more often than each of the other numbers. The numbers 1 to 5 are equally likely to occur.
The die was rolled 1200 times and it was noted that the 6 appeared 450 times.
Which statement is correct?

expectedAnswer.method: Estimate P(6) by 450/1200 = 3/8. The remaining probability is 1 − 3/8 = 5/8, shared equally among five outcomes, so each has estimated probability (5/8)/5 = 1/8. Thus 6 is expected to appear (3/8)/(1/8) = 3 times as often as any one other number.
